subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron runs get explicit `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny`, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or keep the current per-job `toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards model?
rationale: This changes a security-sensitive tool exposure boundary and likely adds or reuses config surface, so source inspection cannot safely choose precedence or upgrade behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add explicit cron policy
options.body: Define `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` precedence against existing global, provider, agent, group, sender, sandbox, subagent, inherited, and per-job `toolsAllow` policies, then update schema, docs, and tests.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat cron runs as inheriting `tools.subagents.tools` where applicable, accepting the simpler model but documenting compatibility impact for existing cron jobs.

options.title: Keep current model
options.body: Leave cron with per-job `--tools` / `toolsAllow` and delivery safeguards only, and document that cron does not have a cron-wide deny policy.

recommendation.title: Add explicit cron policy
recommendation.body: Define `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` precedence against existing global, provider, agent, group, sender, sandbox, subagent, inherited, and per-job `toolsAllow` policies, then update schema, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice spans config schema, tool-policy precedence, subagent/session classification, and cron runner behavior where steipete has the strongest recent current-main history.
